messages:
alex: seeing a spike in TLS handshake failures in eu (~04:15 UTC). errors look like KMS unwrap denies intermittently, not a full outage but lots of degraded requests
megan: saw a surge of 503s from model-serving around the same time, traces show 'tls: write alert: internal error' on the proxy side :eyes:
tj: can you paste the proxy logs and the KMS audit lines? curious whether this is client cert validation or unwrap failing
alex: here's a couple lines from edge-proxy (redacted):
```
edge-proxy[proxy-85c]: 2026-03-23T04:16:02Z error: unwrap failed svc=scheduler-eu err=403 KMSDecryptDenied principal=svc-account:scheduler-eu
edge-proxy[proxy-85c]: 2026-03-23T04:16:02Z tls: write alert: internal error
edge-proxy[proxy-85c]: 2026-03-23T04:16:03Z error: unwrap failed svc=batch-replicator err=403 KMSDecryptDenied principal=svc-account:batch-replicator
```
lina: auditship shows an RBAC change landed 2026-03-22 23:40 UTC — a role-binding that added infra team read access but we also have a higher-priority deny rule for 'keystore:unwrap' in the global policy. sounds like precedence flip causing intermittent allow/deny depending on evaluation order
megan: confirmed. KMS audit entries show alternating 200 and 403 for same keyID and different principals. looks like role-binding churn + deny precedence.
tj: quick mitigations: 1) revert the role-binding change 2) add explicit allow for kms:decrypt to scheduler-eu service-account 3) temporarily enable cached unwrap fallback in the runtime
alex: trying option 2 now — command I'm running: 
```
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: keystore-unwrap-allow-scheduler-eu
  namespace: infra
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: scheduler-eu
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: keystore-unwrap-allow
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
EOF
```
oncall: patching rolebinding to add explicit allow for scheduler-eu (will monitor). ETA ~5m :thumbsup:
sec-bot: automated-alert: keystore-decrypt-failures exceeded threshold in eu at 2026-03-23T04:18:10Z. incident INC-184123 created
megan: also enabling verbose audit for keystore on rotator for 30m: PROBE flag set --audit-level=verbose so we can capture full decision logs
tj: note: check KMS key versioning/rotation history too — if a key version was flagged or removed, some clients might get different behavior and surface 403s from backend HSM during rotation windows
alex: KMS logs show calls from principals: scheduler-eu, batch-replicator, edge-proxy. batch-replicator was added as new SA yesterday in the infra rollout — could be related
lina: post-incident followups: 1) audit precedence rules and tighten deny usage 2) add integration test to validate unwrap path across RBAC permutations 3) add cached unwrap fallback for 30s to reduce impact during transient auth flips 4) add explicit allow-mapping for critical runtime service-accounts (scheduler-eu, edge-proxy) 5) create a playbook for quick rolebinding rollback
megan: short-term global mitigation idea: set edge-proxy env PROXY_ACCEPT_CACHED_INTERMEDIATE=true to accept cached unwrapped material for 60s, reduces outage surface while we sort RBAC
oncall: rolebinding patch applied. monitoring dashboard shows handshake failures falling back to baseline over the last 2m. leaving live for 30m and will schedule a rollback if anything odd
lina: created ticket SEC-2026-112 to track follow-ups, assigned to infra + platform. adding notes about audit-logship parsing and KMS decision granularity
tj: thanks for the quick ops. next steps: ensure KMS policy changes require a canary and add smoke tests that simulate keystore:unwrap calls from all critical principals across regions
alex: will follow up with a short blameless writeup once we confirm stability. thanks everyone :heart:
